question_text: A government memorandum states: 'Only if an applicant possesses a valid Civil Service Eligibility can they be appointed to a career position in the bureaucracy.' Which of the following conclusions logically follows from this statement?

options.text: If an applicant is appointed to a career position, then they possess a valid Civil Service Eligibility.
If an applicant possesses a valid Civil Service Eligibility, then they will be appointed to a career position.
An applicant who does not possess a valid Civil Service Eligibility can still be appointed to a career position if they have relevant experience.
Possessing a valid Civil Service Eligibility is sufficient for appointment to a career position.
